profile.reading: This is the original building of xAI's Colossus supercomputer campus in South Memphis, at 3231 Riverport Road. The site is a former Electrolux appliance factory (785,000 square feet), purchased by Phoenix Investors in December 2023 for $35 million; its existing shell and proximity to wastewater treatment infrastructure and the Mississippi River let xAI complete construction in roughly 122 days, versus an industry-standard multi-year timeline, with Dell Technologies and Supermicro handling infrastructure and Nvidia supplying GPU hardware. xAI, incorporated by Elon Musk in March 2023, finalized its decision to build in Memphis in March 2024, announced the project publicly in June 2024, began operations in July 2024, and officially launched Colossus with 100,000 GPUs in September 2024, primarily to train xAI's Grok chatbot while also supporting X (formerly Twitter) and SpaceX workloads. By June 2025 the GPU count had grown to roughly 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 units, with power consumption rising from about 150 MW at launch to a 250 MW maximum, an amount well beyond the facility's original 150 MW grid connection, so xAI has supplemented it with 35 gas turbines (422 MW combined capacity) and 168 Tesla Megapack batteries. That gas-turbine buildout drew significant environmental scrutiny: the Southern Environmental Law Center has characterized the facility as likely the largest industrial emitter of nitrogen oxides in Memphis, citing an estimated 1,200 to 2,000 tons of NOx annually, and xAI initially operated the turbines without permits under a Shelby County regulatory loophole covering only generators on-site 365-plus days, before EPA standards revised in January 2026 required permits for large temporary methane turbines. Water usage (an expected 5 million-plus gallons daily) and local arsenic-contamination concerns prompted an approved $80 million wastewater recycling facility. No formal public review process preceded the project's announcement, and Memphis residents have reported chronic respiratory issues and learned of the facility primarily from local news coverage rather than a community process.

reading.body:
Colossus 1 is the original building of xAI's Memphis supercomputer campus, a converted 785,000-square-foot appliance factory completed in 122 days and operational since July 2024. The facility launched with 100,000 GPUs in September 2024 and has expanded to approximately 230,000 units as of June 2025, comprising roughly 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 processors. At a typical power draw of 1 kW per GPU, the published 250 MW peak consumption aligns with this scale, though the campus operates well beyond the original 150 MW grid connection through 35 gas turbines providing 422 MW combined capacity and 168 Tesla Megapacks for load management.

The facility qualifies to support large-scale AI training and inference workloads through its dense GPU configuration and redundant power infrastructure. xAI operates Colossus primarily to train its Grok chatbot while supporting X and SpaceX computational demands. The environmental footprint is substantial: an estimated 1,200 to 2,000 tons of nitrogen oxides annually from on-site turbines, expected water usage exceeding 5 million gallons daily managed through an $80 million wastewater recycling system, and local concerns about arsenic contamination from groundwater.

In Tennessee, this campus ranks fifth among four facilities with published megawatt figures, meaning it substantially exceeds all others combined; the state has 24 mapped facilities total, most publishing no capacity data. The rapid construction timeline and reliance on temporary backup generation reflect the speed of infrastructure deployment for large AI compute clusters, while the permitting gaps and environmental scrutiny highlight the mismatch between facility deployment timelines and regulatory frameworks in the jurisdictions where grid capacity remains the binding constraint on scaling.
